headline: A 41-country paper reports a shift toward senior workers at AI-adopting multinationals
summary: A September 2026 Stanford Digital Economy Lab working paper analyzes 1.25 billion job postings and 154 million employment records across 41 countries, inferring firm AI adoption from generative-AI job advertisements. In an instrumented event study of foreign multinational affiliates, the authors report a 1.9-percentage-point decline in junior workforce share by March 2026 relative to matched controls. Senior employment rises 6.7%; the 2.5% decline estimate for junior employment is not statistically significant, and total employment rises 3.3% at marginal significance. The authors interpret their model-based decomposition as suggestive of modest, seniority-biased productivity gains. These are paper-reported estimates, not independent replication or a representative global labor census. The paper notes platform coverage and adoption-timing limits and an untestable instrument exclusion restriction. Its population and adoption measure differ from Anthropic’s October 2026 internal workforce report, so it is comparative evidence rather than a replication.
